OVERVIEW

Abstract

Masked skeleton modeling has recently shown strong potential for self-supervised 3D action representation learning. Existing methods typically follow the masked autoencoder paradigm, where visible skeleton tokens and learnable mask tokens are jointly processed by a self-attention decoder for coordinate or motion reconstruction. However, such a decoder introduces dense interactions among masked tokens, although these interactions may be unnecessary for learning discriminative skeleton representations. In this paper, we propose Multi-order Motion Cross-attention Masked Autoencoder (MoCMAE), a simple yet effective framework for skeleton masked motion pretraining. MoCMAE replaces the conventional self-attention decoder with a masked-query cross-attention decoder, where reconstruction queries attend only to visible encoder tokens, reducing decoder dependency among masked tokens and encouraging the encoder to learn more global motion representations. To better exploit the visible context, we further introduce an encoder multi-layer feature aggregation module (EMFA) that adaptively integrates representations from different encoder layers for reconstruction. In addition, a multi-order motion reconstruction objective is designed to capture complementary temporal dynamics by jointly modeling velocity and acceleration patterns. Extensive experiments show that MoCMAE achieves competitive or superior performance over strong masked motion modeling baselines, especially under high masking ratios, while introducing negligible parameter overhead and reducing decoder computation.

Overall Framework

THE METHOD

Core Theoretical Insights

Three complementary designs make masked motion reconstruction an encoder-driven learning task.

01

Masked-query
cross-attention

Masked tokens act as queries. Keys and values come only from visible encoder features, removing direct interactions among masked tokens.

02

Encoder multi-layer
feature aggregation

Each decoder layer learns to combine features from different encoder depths, bringing local motion details and higher-level context into reconstruction.

03

Multi-order
motion reconstruction

Velocity provides the primary reconstruction target. Acceleration adds complementary supervision for changes in motion dynamics.

ATTENTION-MAP COMPLEXITY

L²versusr(1 − r)L²

At a masking ratio of 95%, the cross-attention map contains 4.75% as many entries as a full self-attention map. This comparison concerns attention-map size, rather than total model FLOPs.
